card.name: Etymology and foreign-language name glosses
card.fires_on: Marks where a foreign-language form is about to appear: the end of a language name (Old Frisian, West Frisian), a colon after a language label, or the start of a transliterated name. It also fires on odd pieces inside URLs and codes.

modes.label: Language names in etymologies
modes.description: The end of a language name or an asterisk just before a cognate word in a word-origin note.

modes.label: Colon before native-script name
modes.description: A colon after a language label, right before the name written in another script.

modes.label: Broken-up names and codes
modes.description: A single letter or piece at the start of a name, web address or code.
modes.example: Check out http://www<<.n>>unnstronger.com for more info

card.writes: It adds a push toward Chinese words and name-like pieces and away from code identifiers, so the effect is weak and mixed.
card.plain: It lights up when text is about to give a word or name in another language, as in word-origin notes.
